| [CLAIM-859](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-859.md) | In two distinct mechanisms that mix a structured step with a uniform one, preferential attachment or copying with a uniform share and noisy sample-space reduction, the tail's survival exponent is one over the structured share | Two mechanisms the record now holds readings for mix a structured step with a uniform one. In noisy sample-space reduction (Corominas-Murtra et al., [THEORY-2175](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2175.md)), a step is nested with probability λ and uniform otherwise, occupation falls as i^−λ in rank, and the frequency exponent is 1 + 1/λ, so the survival exponent is 1/λ. In both the survival exponent is one over the share of structured steps: structure alone gives the marginal exponent 1, and the uniform share sets how far the tail is diluted from it. This is a pattern across two mechanisms, offered as a candidate row for [QUESTION-505](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-505.md), not a theorem; whether it reaches past processes of this mixed form is not shown.
